blocks.text: Sort-then-two-pointers is valid when reordering or copying and O(n log n) time are acceptable, but it is not universally dominant. For the hash alternative, scan x in original order, first test whether T - x is already in the set, and only then insert x. Query-before-insert prevents one occurrence from pairing with itself while still allowing two equal occurrences to match on the second one. This gives expected O(n) time and O(n) worst-case auxiliary space under the stated hash assumption. The decision can reverse under strict memory limits, adversarial hash guarantees, or repeated operations that reuse sorted order.
